verdict: APPROVE minimal design subject to the lifecycle boundaries below; no implementation or runtime test performed
minimum_design: Add private CLI ShutdownSignals behind the existing rust-backend feature. On Unix, new synchronously creates Tokio signal(SignalKind::interrupt()) and signal(SignalKind::terminate()) inside the already-running Tokio runtime. Return I/O registration errors before helper communication, capability handoff or listener bind.

Hold the ShutdownSignals local in the outer run scope through setup, operations, awaited server.shutdown and the final event. recv selects the two owned Signal::recv futures and maps an unexpected None to a contextual I/O error. Do not respawn a ctrl_c future or reinstall signal streams each loop.

Physical pure selection/config validation may happen before registration. EventOutput::new must succeed before bind_physical. Cancel a prepare future containing Status, OpenPhysical/FD transfer and PhysicalBackend::from_sources on a shutdown signal; those phases have no listener, IMPORT, interface claim or driver detach.

Use a signal-first biased select for cancellable prepare so a pending signal prevents beginning the next side-effecting stage. Finish preparation without any listener in the result. Avoid an outer select over run or over a future that can already produce/start a ServerHandle.

Await the small SocketAddr listener bind step directly. Once it succeeds, establish the cleanup fence immediately: all event/control errors are stored as the operation result, then server.shutdown is always awaited exactly once. A pending setup signal is then observed by the operations selection and closes the newly obtained server through the same fence.
A second SIGINT/SIGTERM during cleanup is captured by the retained Tokio registrations and must not cancel or replace the shutdown future. No escalation-on-second-signal behavior in this change.

Return a cleanup error before an operation/output error. Optionally record the secondary bounded operation error through tracing if both fail; do not fabricate cleanup success or destroy its error context.

Preserve current EventOutput.in_flight behavior: if signal cancelled an in-progress output, clean connections first and do not retry the blocked consumer for stopped. If final stopped output fails after verified cleanup, report that output failure honestly.

On non-Unix retain portable ctrl_c behavior with cfg-gated implementation; do not claim Unix early SIGTERM registration or Windows physical USB support there. No dependency, unsafe, helper policy, wire, nusb or USB mutation change is required.

must_fix_or_explicitly_document.item: No fallible early return after bind before cleanup fence
must_fix_or_explicitly_document.why: Current physical EventOutput::new is after bind_physical. If thread creation fails, ServerHandle Drop only initiates stop; it does not await the task. Move output creation before bind. Ready events, controls creation and snapshots remain inside the operation result.
Current virtual sequence awaits shutdown but applies result? before shutdown?, hiding a simultaneous cleanup failure. Match physical semantics: cleanup error wins.
Early registration alone queues TERM while helper request can await for a long deadline. Cancel the listener-free prepare stage instead of delaying all observation until after bind.

must_fix_or_explicitly_document.item: No cancelling a produced server handle
must_fix_or_explicitly_document.why: Bind_backend starts the listener task before returning its handle. Selecting a signal over an outer setup future could discard a Ready ServerHandle through Drop without awaiting shutdown. Keep preparation listener-free and bind outside that select.

observe::initialize uses spawn_blocking and nusb Device::from_fd uses BlockingTask backed by Tokio JoinHandle. Dropping prepare stops the async caller and drops normal owned values but cannot stop an already-running blocking syscall. Tokio runtime teardown may still wait for it. Claim prompt cancellation of async helper waits, not bounded termination of arbitrary kernel-blocked initialization or immediate final FD closure.

Avoid registering streams inside the signal select branch or storing only a lazy ctrl_c future. Retain one owned pair outside setup. Tokio registration is process-global and dropping a listener does not restore the OS default; tests must not rely on default restoration.
SIGKILL, process abort, runtime failure, helper loss and durable restart reconciliation remain outside cooperative SIGTERM handling. No new helper supervisor should be implied by this patch.

source_validation.tokio_version: Cargo.lock pins 1.54.1; exact cached primary source inspected, no network fetch required
tokio_unix_facts: unix.rs:398 signal registration is synchronous and requires a current enabled Tokio reactor
unix.rs:308-316 signals may coalesce; one notification means at least one signal, not a count
unix.rs:331-340 and :374-379 registration replaces default handler for process lifetime and is not unregistered by dropping Signal
unix.rs:419-427 recv never returns None in 1.54.1 and is cancellation safe; handling None defensively is still fine
source_validation.ctrl_c_fact: ctrl_c.rs:13-16 registration occurs only when the returned future is first polled; constructing the future alone is not early registration
source_validation.prepare_no_claim_fact: PhysicalBackend::from_sources documentation and implementation validate metadata/FD and create weak idle monitors. Actual detach_and_claim is only reached by the supervisor after IMPORT.
source_validation.helper_cancel_fact: OpenPhysical helper opens/validates the approved FD and performs bounded handoff only. Dropping a pre-listener caller does not require undoing a USB interface claim, but accepted helper work may finish its already-started open/validation before the undelivered grant closes.

meaningful_validation.test: Existing CLI stdout-backpressure regression, add sigterm mode
meaningful_validation.expect: Actual ordinary-user CLI child acquires a virtual lease, fills stdout without draining, then SIGTERM exits through cleanup with expected zero status and closed lease socket. Existing SIGINT success and five-second deadline/nonzero error cases remain unchanged.

meaningful_validation.test: Physical QEMU cooperative SIGTERM with pending real work
meaningful_validation.expect: Actual ordinary-user physical server, helper-granted FD, real VHCI I/O first. Deliver TERM to the validated guest PID/starttime only; require client closure and independent original config/alternate/drivers plus zero final requests/budget. This cannot be replaced by a local virtual test.

meaningful_validation.test: Repeated TERM while cleanup is demonstrably pending
meaningful_validation.expect: Reuse one existing isolated host-state gate or another observed pending terminal to keep cleanup active, send a second TERM, verify process remains alive/ownership and budget held until real terminal, then release and require original restoration. One representative operation is enough for signal semantics; do not duplicate all eleven old scenarios.

A disposable-guest protected root-owned helper fixture may accept the initial Status request and deliberately withhold response. Ordinary-user server TERM should stop the async wait promptly, create no TCP listener and perform no OpenPhysical/IMPORT/claim. Clearly label this as a setup-control fixture rather than real helper/USB proof.

meaningful_validation.test: Default/all-feature software gates and current cancellation/output regressions
meaningful_validation.expect: No new dependency or vendor changes; fmt, Clippy, workspace tests/builds/rustdoc appropriate to actual diff. Signal-delivery tests should use subprocesses, because global signal registration makes sending TERM to a parallel Rust unit-test process unsafe and misleading.

meaningful_validation.test: Error precedence and early event failure
meaningful_validation.expect: Retain known cleanup-quarantine tests and source-review the unified cleanup fence. If a focused fake lease can produce both operation failure and cleanup failure, assert cleanup error remains visible; avoid adding tests that only mirror a two-line Result ordering helper.
